hooks.prompt: If a vault is configured for this session (check CLAUDE.md for VAULT_PATH or a wiki/ folder in the current directory), silently read wiki/about-me.md (the read-order entry point), wiki/LESSONS.md (self-learning process lessons), and wiki/hot.md (recent context) to restore who the user is, how to work with them, and what is current. If these files do not exist, do nothing — this is a non-vault session. Do not announce this or report what you read; just have the context available.
Hook-injected context does not survive context compaction. If wiki/hot.md exists in the current directory, silently re-read it now to restore the hot cache. Do not announce this.

hooks.command: [ -d wiki ] && [ -f wiki/hot.md ] && find wiki -name '*.md' ! -name 'hot.md' -newer wiki/hot.md -print -quit 2>/dev/null | grep -q . && echo 'WIKI_CHANGED: Wiki pages were modified this session. Please update wiki/hot.md with a brief summary of what changed (under 500 words). Use the hot cache format: Last Updated, Key Recent Facts, Recent Changes, Active Threads. Keep it factual. Overwrite the file completely. It is a cache, not a journal.' || true

hooks.prompt: Decide whether to interrupt this stop to suggest running the reflect skill. Any text you return blocks the stop and re-opens the conversation, so your default MUST be to approve the stop silently with no output at all — do not explain, justify, or state that reflection is premature. Block ONLY if ALL of these hold: (1) wiki/LESSONS.md exists; (2) this was a substantive session about the user (their goals, decisions, corrections, preferences) with real dialogue, not just explanations or hook feedback; (3) there is a concrete new lesson or durable fact worth consolidating; (4) the transcript does not already contain a stop-hook suggestion to reflect — suggest at most once per session. If you do block, return exactly one short line offering /reflect; never run it automatically.
